back: An early working model of a system that users try to find out what they need.
Throwaway: discarded after the requirements are known. Evolutionary: refined until it becomes the final system.
Benefits: early feedback, user involvement. Drawbacks: users think it is nearly finished, untidy design, never-ending changes.
Developing a system as a set of interacting objects, instances of classes.
Class: a template of attributes and methods. Object: one instance of a class.
Nouns in the description suggest classes; verbs suggest methods; facts about nouns suggest attributes.
A subclass takes over the attributes and methods of its parent class, so shared data is defined once.
Shows actors (users) and the use cases (things they do with the system).
Fixed requirements: waterfall. Unclear requirements: prototyping. Reuse and extension: object-oriented.
